messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: new logo
parts:
We never heard back from Stephanie about fonts or color,
so I assume we're on our own at this point.

I suggest we just go with the same bold Helvetica font
for "Stan" that we use on the web page.

I also realized the blue she used was NOT Columbia's
blue, so I'm OK just going with that. Let's talk
at a meeting about it.

I don't think we need to wait until Stan 3 --- no idea
when that'll happen --- it's certainly not on the short-term
horizon. I was hoping we could get black-box VB, MLE, and
RHMC in before we went to Stan 3, but all of those projects
are held up for one reason or another (and they're all held
up by the fact that we still haven't debugged higher-order
autodiff fully).

- Bob

messages.author: 03a00bb0d0e31e74
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] new logo
parts: Some comments, i.e. yeses, below:

On Thu, Feb 19, 2015 at 7:15 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
Would you like to move ShinyStan to the stan-dev repo?

Sure, that would be great. Because of the name change (SHINYstan to shinyStan) the new version I've been working on isn't in the jgabry/SHINYstan repository but rather at shinyStan/shinyStan. The new one is the one we should move to stan-dev. The new version is basically ready to go (I'm just working on some tests) and I was thinking that the presentation at the nyhackR meetup on Wednesday would be a good time to make the new version public (well it's public already I suppose, but not annouced).

Also, would you like us to add you as one of the Stan
core developers?  It looks like Andrew wants to lean
pretty heavily on ShinyStan going forward!

I would be honored. You guys have really done an amazing job and Stan is such an important contribution to statistics and every other field that relies on statistics. Working on shinyStan is by far the most enjoyable work I've been doing and I'd love to work with you in whatever capacity helps Stan moving forward. 
 
Jonah
